subject: Clarify: Data residency + 'no training' assurance and retention edge cases
content:
From: Priya Sood <privacy@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: confirm you "don't train on customer text" + retention nuance

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for walking us through the integration yesterday. Legal asked for a couple of clarifications before we move to procurement:

1) We need a plain-English confirmation that Redwood will not use Acme customer text to train or fine-tune any models (including internal research), unless Acme explicitly opts in.
2) Please explain what you mean by "ephemeral" caches vs "backups/snapshots" and the practical delete window for each. Our security team is concerned about debug snapshots and cold backups that might be stored outside the usual retention window.

If you have a one-page or diagram we can hand to Legal, that would be perfect.

Appreciate it,
Priya
Priya Sood
Senior Privacy Counsel, Acme Corp
privacy@acme-corp.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sood <privacy@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ian Lee <ian.lee@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: confirm you "don't train on customer text" + retention nuance

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front:

- We will not use Acme customer content to train, fine-tune, or update any production models or downstream model checkpoints unless Acme signs an explicit data-sharing opt-in. That includes both automated training pipelines and manual researcher experiments.

- For retention: runtime artifacts (request payloads, transient KV cache entries, and token-level inference traces used for routing/batching) are treated as ephemeral: they are held in memory or short-lived storage and are eligible for deletion within 0–30 days depending on config. Backups, snapshots, and debug archives are retained only per contract and are not used for modeling. Standard hosted defaults: ephemeral cache 0–7 days, operational logs 30 days, snapshots/archival backups 90 days unless otherwise specified.

I attached a one-pager and a simple process diagram that Legal often finds useful. Let me loop in our privacy and security SMEs to make sure legal gets precise language for contract clauses.

Attachment: redwood_nontraining_one-pager.pdf (PDF, 28KB)
Attachment: erase-process-diagram.png (PNG, 120KB)

Best,
Jordan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@ben.carter>
Date: Sat, 12 Apr 2025 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick Q: confirm you "don't train on customer text" + retention nuance

Jordan/Marissa/Ben — happy to take this. Draft language below is intentionally conservative for Legal:

1) Non-Training Assurance (proposed): "Redwood Inference will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve any of Redwood's production models, research models, or internal model checkpoints, unless Customer provides an explicit, written opt-in that describes the scope and duration of the use. This commitment covers automated training pipelines, manual experiments, and any derivative model artifacts."

2) Retention and Deletion (proposed): "Runtime artifacts (including request payloads, ephemeral KV cache entries, and short-lived inference traces) are stored only for operational purposes and are eligible for automatic deletion within a default window of 0–7 days for ephemeral caches and up to 30 days for operational logs. Persistent snapshots, backups, or debug archives are considered archival and are retained up to 90 days under standard hosted terms; longer retention may apply only pursuant to explicit contract language. Neither archival backups nor ephemeral artifacts are used for model training or evaluation unless Customer explicitly opts in."

3) Backups & Disaster Recovery: "In rare disaster-recovery scenarios we may restore backups to recover Customer service; such restores are limited to data recovery activities and are not used to extract signals for model training. Restored data is subject to the same deletion and tombstoning procedures."

4) Evidence & Auditing: "Upon request, Redwood will provide an attestation of non-training and relevant retention logs. For enterprise customers, we can incorporate non-training guarantees and specific deletion SLAs into the contract and DocuSign annex."

If Legal wants more conservative time windows we can tighten numbers, but these are the operationally realistic defaults that match our current runtime and backup schedules.

— Rishi
Privacy & Policy

Hi Priya / Ian — Following up with the conservative language Rishi suggested. Summary for Legal: we will provide the full draft wording (below) in the contract addendum; we can shorten or tighten retention windows if Acme requires it as part of the deal.

Quoted draft for contract: 
"Redwood Inference will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve any of Redwood's production or research models, or derive any new models from Customer Content, unless Customer provides an explicit, written opt-in that defines scope and duration. Runtime artifacts (request payloads, KV cache entries and inference traces) are eligible for deletion within 0–7 days by default; operational logs are retained up to 30 days. Backups, snapshots, and debug archives are retained up to 90 days under standard terms and are not used for model training. Restores for disaster recovery are limited to data-recovery activities and are not used for model improvement. Redwood will provide attestation evidence on request and will incorporate non-training guarantees and retention SLAs into enterprise contracts."
Next steps: Please let me know if Legal wants alternate windows (e.g., 0–3 days for ephemeral caches, 0 days for KV cache TTL) and we can update the addendum. If OK, I'll attach the signed DocuSign clause to the SOW.

Best,
Jordan
